text: Language models predict the next token from a sequence. A token can be a word, part of a word, or punctuation. Training compares predicted probabilities with the next token in the data. The resulting loss measures how well those predictions fit the text. A tiny demonstration checks this process; it does not teach broad knowledge or reliable instruction following.

A dataset supplies the examples a model learns from. Before training, inspect where the text came from and which permissions allow its use. Remove empty documents and repeated material. Keep separate validation and test documents so that evaluation asks the model to predict text it did not see during training. These example paragraphs were written for this repository.

A tokenizer maps text into integer token identifiers. Byte-level tokenization can represent unfamiliar characters using bytes. Byte pair encoding learns frequent combinations from the training documents. The vocabulary determines how the model represents text and influences sequence length. Keep the tokenizer with every checkpoint because the weights depend on the exact token identifiers.

A neural network starts with randomly initialized parameters. Each training update computes predictions, evaluates a loss, calculates gradients and adjusts trainable weights. The optimizer applies those updates using a learning rate. A short run can validate numerical behavior and checkpoint recovery. Useful model quality requires suitable data, sufficient training and careful evaluation.

Attention lets a decoder use information from earlier tokens. A causal mask prevents each position from reading future tokens while predicting the next one. Positional information helps the network distinguish different orders. Grouped query attention shares key and value representations between groups of heads. Architecture choices affect capacity, compute and memory consumption.

Model checkpoints preserve weights and optimizer state. Saving random generator state makes recovery reproducible when the data and configuration also match. Keep manifests describing the bytes used in the run. A resumed experiment should reuse its saved data rather than quietly acquire a different corpus. Recovery tests compare subsequent results with uninterrupted training.

Evaluation should match the purpose of the model. Next token loss and perplexity describe prediction on held out text. Task benchmarks test narrower abilities such as selecting a plausible continuation. A tiny sample is useful for software checks and does not establish a reliable quality ranking. Record sample size and scoring protocol beside every reported result.

Instruction tuning uses pairs of prompts and useful responses. The training objective can mask prompt tokens so that the loss focuses on the answer. This differs from broad next token pretraining on raw documents. Data quality matters at every stage. Short examples illustrate the format but a capable assistant needs appropriate coverage and much more training.

A learning rate controls the size of optimizer updates. Too large an update can destabilize training. A schedule may warm up the learning rate and gradually decrease it. Gradient clipping limits very large gradients. Mixed precision can reduce memory and improve speed on suitable hardware. Check numerical behavior rather than assuming a faster configuration is always better.

Inference generates new tokens from a prompt using the trained model. Temperature changes the sharpness of the probability distribution. Sampling can produce different outputs even from the same input. Context length bounds the amount of text the model can read at once. Keep generation limits explicit so that interactive use has predictable resource consumption.

Cloud execution moves a declared workload to another machine. A controller should validate local inputs, estimate spending and retain a recoverable launch record. Temporary training instances need termination and cleanup checks. Persistent API hosting has a different lifecycle and keeps running until explicitly stopped or deleted. Monitor storage costs as well as compute costs.

A model export packages the configuration, tokenizer and weights for an inference runtime. Serving through an API adds operational concerns such as authentication, encrypted transport and request limits. A local demonstration can check model loading and generation without exposing a network service. Public deployment requires its own review and realistic load testing.
